cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the hall key in my teacup like you. The wedding invitation can sit underneath; everything for getting in, together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My cup was empty. Yours still has tea in it, and the key's dropped to the bottom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, all in one place. Use the invitation to dry the key when you fish it out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The paper's stuck in the key's teeth. I can peel it away, but the printed address is coming off with it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read the address to me before you peel. Then put the clean key in the empty cup; I'll have to carry the invitation in my head.

reason: Make the joined key/address conflict force an actual ordered rescue—memorize before peeling—then return cup and invitation in altered roles without a thematic summary.
